appearance_facts.fact: The May bar is the shortest of all six bars, reaching only a small fraction of the y-axis scale (well below the 10,000 gridline). It is visibly far shorter than the next-lowest bar (Jun, ~17,500) and dramatically shorter than the tallest (Jan, 40,000).
Apr (~29,500), Jan (40,000), Jun (~17,500), Feb (20,000), Mar (~26,800), May (lowest, ~8,000). May is an extreme outlier low relative to every other month.
All six bars are the same dark red; no special color or marker distinguishes May from the others.

printed_facts.fact: Month; categories in left-to-right order: Apr, Jan, Jun, Feb, Mar, May
No numeric annotation printed on the May bar; its top sits below the 10,000 gridline (visually ≈8,000 kWh).

public_definitions: Routing criterion: Whether May should be handled as a standard low-output case or as a critical anomaly.
Option 1: Route May to standard low-output follow-up.
Option 2: Escalate May to critical low-output anomaly review.
Option 3: Send May to background monthly record filing.
uncertain: No explicit numeric threshold or policy table defines the boundary between 'standard low-output' and 'critical anomaly'; the decision rests on judging May's value as an outlier.
May's exact kWh value is not printed; it is read visually as below 10,000 (≈8,000).
